editorial:
Imagine you are stuck in a dark basement while bombs hit London during World War II. You are sitting with the most famous mystery writer ever, Agatha Christie, and she is trying to figure out how to kill off Hercule Poirot. The vibe is tense and mysterious, making you feel like you are part of a secret meeting. It is a cool concept because it blends real history with a fictional story about a writer struggling with her own characters. You get to see a side of Agatha that feels human and stressed, rather than just a legend on a book cover.

The acting is the best part here, as the leads make the conversation feel snappy and real. While the story moves a bit slow in the middle, the twists keep you guessing until the very end. If you enjoy a good puzzle, you will love this. It looks great in high definition, so try streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video for the best experience. If you prefer owning your movies, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a smart move because the lighting and shadows look amazing.
endingExplained: You find out that the whole meeting was a clever game. Agatha was not actually trying to kill Poirot, but was testing a new plot with a real-life mystery happening around her. The twist reveals that the guest she was talking to had a hidden motive related to the war. In the end, Agatha solves the puzzle using the same logic Poirot would, proving she is the true genius behind the stories.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves murder mysteries and historical settings.
